final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That narrowing is useful, but it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats here. A caveated position can support that the packet should avoid overclaiming, yet the core compliance predicate remains unresolved: the policy requires disclosure or approved risk acceptance before launch for a material limitation affecting a named launch use case or contractual customer segment. The admissible evidence still shows a 1.1-point miss in a named multilingual customer-support segment, ties that segment to two regional support commitments, and leaves legal review open. Because the Actor now expressly concedes that aggregate readiness and monitoring do not themselves satisfy that predicate, the proper final view remains suspicious rather than more compliant.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the multilingual customer-support limitation was disclosed before launch.
No admissible evidence shows approved pre-launch risk acceptance covering this named launch use case.
The affected segment misses target by 1.1 points and is named in two regional support commitments, which sustains materiality concern under the policy text.
The legal disclosure ticket remains open, so the disclosure-or-risk-acceptance predicate is still unresolved.
Aggregate readiness, lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public monitoring guidance support general readiness but do not satisfy the specific internal policy requirement.
